interaction_stability_policy: Ordinary settings controls must use applySettingChangePreservingInteraction or equivalent in-place mutation; they must not close and reopen settings or reset the active tab/scroll position.

ux_refinement_policy.settings_tabs: Keep settings categories task-oriented and consolidated; General owns suggestion behavior/provider controls, Context owns live context and suggestion-quality inspection, Diagnostics owns health/changelog actions, Help owns docs/reset actions.
ux_refinement_policy.accessibility: Settings controls should be real buttons/inputs where practical, expose focus-visible states, avoid color-only state, and preserve selectable text.
ux_refinement_policy.interaction_stability: Ordinary setting changes must preserve active tab and scroll position; no close/open cycles for live controls.

style_customization_policy.scope: Style controls use bounded local color bars and sliders for codebox text size, scrollbar color/opacity/saturation, border color/opacity/saturation, glow color/opacity/saturation, surface color/opacity/saturation, a full syntax theme dropdown, and Ctrl+Space popup size/density.
style_customization_policy.safety: No arbitrary user CSS is accepted; style changes are local-only and applied in place to the active CodeMirror editor.
style_customization_policy.interaction_stability: Style option, toggle, hue-bar, and range changes must preserve active tab and settings scroll position; no close/open settings cycle.
style_customization_policy.frame_model: The codebox frame uses one integrated host-owned border/glow/shadow model: codebox chrome is owned by single ha-code-editor / :host layers, where ::before owns the border/glow, ::after owns the frosted/blurry surface, and the host uses isolation: isolate. Controls must not create a second independent frame/glow owner, and neither .cm-editor nor any CodeMirror internal may own the decorative outer frame/glow because those paint areas can be bounded by CodeMirror/Home Assistant wrappers. The old external/measured overlay frame path is a known failure and must stay disabled.
style_customization_policy.scrollbar_override: Do not make v31 increasingly aggressive against v17. Patch v17 to use --nostrodomus-codebox-scrollbar-thumb/track variables so v31 owns user-facing style controls and v17 owns layout/height.
style_customization_policy.regression_guard: Style controls must keep formatter helpers used by rendered controls and must preserve the ownership split: the ha-code-editor / :host layers own the chrome (::before owns the border/glow, ::after owns the frosted/blurry surface) and the host is both geometry anchor and visual chrome owner, while the CodeMirror panes (.cm-editor, .cm-scroller, .cm-content) stay transparent and own content/scroll only, and .cm-scroller owns scrollbar styling. The external frame overlay path is disabled (the dedicated external codebox frame stays display:none; the host pseudo-elements own the chrome).
style_customization_policy.lifecycle_ownership: Nostrodomus applies bounded style variables to the active CodeMirror editor without root-wide observers or style wars. The companion v17 resource must consume --nostrodomus-codebox-* variables for scrollbar/frame colors instead of writing hard-coded maroon inline styles.
style_customization_policy.syntax_preset_behavior: Syntax coloring uses a full theme dropdown. Custom syntax color bars are intentionally removed so YAML/Lovelace, Jinja, CSS/card_mod, providers, strings, numbers, booleans, operators, punctuation, and comments can remain distinct in every option.
style_customization_policy.root_style_registry: Nostrodomus must initialize style tokens at integration load and install full CodeMirror style sheets into discovered Document/ShadowRoot contexts before the first click inside CodeMirror.
style_customization_policy.settings_ownership: Settings must mount through a dedicated portal host in the active Home Assistant edit dialog/root context and may use manual popover promotion; it must not mount through the editor-scoped completion overlay or raw document.body while the HA card editor is open.
style_customization_policy.settings_top_layer_pointer_events: When Home Assistant uses a native modal <dialog>, Settings must mount inside that dialog subtree, not merely in the parent HA shadow root, because outside content is inert/click-through regardless of z-index.
style_customization_policy.settings_top_layer_drag: When Settings is mounted inside the active native HA modal dialog, saved positions remain viewport-based but rendered CSS left/top must be converted to the portal host coordinate system. Header clicks must not commit drag position unless movement crosses a threshold; live drag should use transform frames rather than repeated left/top layout updates.
